newsitem.title: ROMANIA: RADIO ROMANIA AFTERNOON HEADLINES AT 1 PM.
newsitem.headline: RADIO ROMANIA AFTERNOON HEADLINES AT 1 PM.

text.p: * Ruling coalition senators voted to upkeep a decision by the former parliament to strip Greater Romania Party senator Corneliu Vadim Tudor of his parliamentary immunity on suspicions of calumny in his weekly Romania Mare.
Opposition senators walked out, saying the procedure breached the constitution and Senate regulations.
Opposition Party of Social Democracy leader Oliviu Gherman said his party would contest the decision with the Constitutional Court.
* Lower Chamber of Deputies voted a law on forensic institutes allowing their decentralisation and privatisation.
* Prime Minister Victor Ciorbea met Hungarian businessmen during the second day of his official visit to Budapest.
He is expected to visit Hungarian key enterprises Videoton and Ikarus.

* Romania and Hungary will boost trade and economic cooperation this year following the conclusion in April of an accord on Romania's joining the Central European Free Trade Association, Industry and Trade Minister Calin Tariceanu said in Budapest.
He said the Romanian delegation discussed convertibility between the Hungarian forint currency and Romania's leu.

* Romania and Hungary want to resume traditional economic cooperation, Tariceanu said. He said Hungarian bus maker Ikarus would resume trade with Romania, while Romanian rolling stock manufacturers would make exports to their neighbours.

* National Unity Party (PUNR) protested against a recent declaration by Ciorbea saying the Cluj-based Babes-Bolyai Unitersity was to split into a Hungarian-language Bolyai university and a Romanian-language section named Babes.

* The Hungarian-language university could open as early as this autumn, leaders of the local branch of the Hungarian Democratic Union (UDMR) said. They said the university would be open for Romanian students and professors, provided they are profficient in Hungarian.
* The rector and deputy rector of the Babes-Bolyai University slammed separation plans, saying the move would create social problems and acrimony over splitting asssets.
* Leaders of the ruling National Liberal Party, the Democratic Party and the UDMR said they favoured the creation of a Hungarian-language university in Cluj.
* Romania is on the right path to achieve NATO integration, said Franklin Kramer, assistant to the U.S. Defence Secretary.
He said the Balkan country would play an essential role in the region's security and stability together with Poland and Hungary.
